transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you tell me what brings you in to see me?

Well… I guess I’ve been forgetting things I shouldn’t. Appointments, like heart follow-ups, calling the clinic back. Sometimes I’ll go to do a repair and realize I didn’t bring the right tools. It’s been happening enough that… I figured I should come in.
When did you first start noticing these memory lapses, and how long has this been going on?

It’s been… maybe a little over a year. About a year and two months, I guess. It got to be more of a real problem after that heart scare, when I had to cut back on my walking and the projects I used to keep busy with.
Over this past year, have you also been feeling unusually sad, worried, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?
I don’t know… not really unusually sad, no. Worried maybe some, but I figure that’s normal with health stuff. I still like doing things, just… I haven’t been doing as much.
Since these memory lapses began, would you say they've been gradually getting worse over time, or have they stayed about the same since they first started?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I notice it more now, but I can’t say if it’s actually getting worse or if I’m just paying more attention to it. It’s been kind of there.

Have these memory lapses caused you to need help from others with everyday tasks—like managing your finances, taking medications correctly, or handling household chores—that you used to do on your own?

A little, yeah. I still do most things myself, but… the senior-center repair group can’t really count on me like they used to. And my doctor’s office has had to call after me about heart follow-ups I missed. So, yeah, it’s caused some trouble.
Besides forgetting things, have you noticed any new difficulty finding the right words when speaking, getting confused about the day or time, or getting lost in places you know well?
Not really, no. I mean… I lose my train of thought sometimes, but I haven’t noticed getting lost or not knowing what day it is. Words… I don’t think that’s been a big problem.

Do you notice your memory or thinking troubles get worse specifically around times when your heart symptoms flare up—like chest pain, shortness of breath, or fatigue—or do they seem to happen independently of how your heart is doing that day?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed a pattern like that. It seems to just happen… kind of on its own, not something I’ve really tied to my heart acting up.
Aside from memory, have you noticed any new difficulty concentrating, following conversations, or planning and organizing tasks like you used to?

Yeah… some concentrating, I guess. Like I’ll sit down at the bridge table, or at one of the Fix-It Friends planning meetings, meaning to follow along, and after a bit my mind just sort of slips off. Then I realize I missed a good chunk of what people were saying.
Thinking back, did you first notice these memory and concentration problems starting suddenly around the time of your heart scare, or had you already begun noticing them before that happened?

I think it was more after the heart scare, yeah. Not all at once exactly, but since then… maybe a little over a year now. About a year and a couple months, I guess. Once I had to cut back on my walking and the projects that kept me busy, it started causing more real trouble.

I don’t really know. I mean, I get tired sometimes, but I haven’t noticed anything clear like that lining up with the memory stuff. Nothing I can point to for sure.

Since your heart scare, have people close to you mentioned that your personality or the way you react emotionally seems different than before—like being more irritable, impulsive, or 'not quite yourself'?

Maybe a little. I don’t know if I’d call it personality exactly, but… I do butt in more than I should. If folks are talking about a project, or even a card hand nearby, I’ll jump in with what I think before anyone asks me. Then afterward I realize I kind of barged in.
Would you say this tendency to interrupt or blurt out your thoughts happens most of the time now, in many different situations, or is it just occasional?

It’s… more than occasional, I guess. Not every minute, but it comes up in different places. If I hear people talking about a project or even a card hand, I’ll jump in with my opinion before anybody asks. Then afterward I can tell I barged in.

Besides jumping into conversations, have you noticed yourself making impulsive decisions—like spending money, agreeing to things, or starting projects—without thinking through the consequences the way you used to?
I don’t think so. I mean… not in any big way that I’ve noticed. I might decide something quicker than I used to, but I can’t really point to spending or taking on projects like that.

Have the people close to you—like your card-playing friends or the Fix-It Friends group—reacted to this blurting out, such as seeming annoyed, distancing themselves, or commenting that you're not acting like your usual self?

Some of them have, yeah. Not in a big dramatic way, but… the repair group at the senior center, I don’t think they count on me like they used to. And my doctor’s office has had to call after me about missing heart follow-ups. So… I guess it’s causing some problems.
Have you noticed your moods shifting more quickly or intensely than before—like sudden irritability, unusual cheerfulness, or getting upset more easily than used to be typical for you?
I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed my moods doing that. I might get a little irritated now and then, but nothing that feels unusual to me.
Would you say this tendency to blurt things out or act impulsively shows up across most areas of your life now—not just at card games or repair meetings—like at home or in other social settings?

Yeah… I suppose it does a bit. If I hear people talking about a project, or even a card hand nearby, I’ll jump in with what I think before anyone asks me. Then afterward I realize I kind of barged in.
During your heart scare, did you lose consciousness, stop breathing, or have anyone tell you that your heart stopped or that you had a stroke at that time?
I’m not really sure about all that. I don’t remember anyone saying my heart stopped or that I had a stroke. I don’t think I stopped breathing, but… I wasn’t exactly keeping track.
Between the memory lapses and the tendency to blurt things out or interrupt, which one would you say causes you more trouble day to day?

The forgetting, I’d say. The interrupting gets me embarrassed sometimes, but the memory stuff causes more trouble… missing heart follow-up things, not calling the clinic back, or turning up for a repair without the right tools. That’s more of why I’m here.

Well… it’s mostly the forgetting. I miss things I really shouldn’t, like heart follow-ups or calling the clinic back. And sometimes I’ll turn up to a repair without the right tools. That’s… that’s what brought me in, really.

Like I said, it’s the forgetting. I’ll miss a heart follow-up, forget to call the clinic back, or show up for a repair and realize I didn’t bring what I needed. That’s the part that’s been causing problems.
